summary: LLM inference costs are dominated by token volume, and most production workloads reprocess identical context on every call. Combining prompt caching, retrieval tuning, response/semantic caching, and model routing routinely cuts spend by 50-80% while improving latency. The highest-leverage lever in 2026 is prompt caching, which bills static prompt prefixes at up to 90% off with no change to output quality.

techniques.name: Prompt Caching (KV cache reuse)
techniques.description: Reuse the computed key-value tensors behind a repeated prompt prefix (system prompts, few-shot examples, documents) so the static portion of each request is billed at a steep discount and processed faster. Supported natively by major providers.
techniques.savings: up to 90% reduction on cached prefix tokens; cache-read discounts commonly 75-90%
techniques.example: Put your long static system prompt and tool definitions at the very start of the message array so OpenAI/Anthropic automatic prefix caching kicks in, billing those tokens at ~10-25% of normal cost on subsequent calls.

techniques.name: Semantic Caching
techniques.description: Cache responses keyed by embedding similarity rather than exact string match, so semantically equivalent queries return a stored answer without hitting the model. Best for high-repetition, FAQ-style, or support workloads.
techniques.savings: API call reduction up to 68.8%; up to 73% cost reduction in high-repetition workloads (Redis LangCache)
techniques.example: Route requests through Redis LangCache or GPTCache; a question like 'how do I reset my password?' returns the cached answer for 'password reset steps' at near-zero marginal cost.

techniques.name: Exact-Match Response Caching
techniques.description: Store full responses for identical (deterministic) prompts and serve them directly on repeat requests. Simple, lossless, and ideal for idempotent or templated calls.
techniques.savings: up to 100% reduction on repeated identical calls
techniques.example: Hash the full prompt (with temperature=0) as a Redis key and return the cached completion when the same prompt arrives again.

techniques.name: Model Routing / Cascading
techniques.description: Send easy or low-risk requests to a cheaper, smaller model and escalate only hard queries to a frontier model. A cheap classifier or confidence check decides the tier.
techniques.savings: 50-80% cost reduction depending on traffic mix (a 16x price gap exists between budget and premium tiers)
techniques.example: Use LiteLLM or a RouteLLM policy to send simple classification to GPT-4o-mini or Gemini Flash and only route ambiguous cases to GPT-4o/Claude Opus.

techniques.name: Fix Retrieval Before Touching Wording (RAG tuning)
techniques.description: Improving chunking, reranking, and top-k retrieval reduces the amount of context you stuff into prompts, which cuts tokens more than any prompt-wording change. Only send the most relevant passages.
techniques.savings: 30-70% reduction in input tokens for RAG pipelines
techniques.example: Add a reranker (e.g. Cohere Rerank) and drop top-k from 20 chunks to 4, sending far fewer document tokens per query without hurting answer quality.

techniques.name: Prompt Compression / Trimming
techniques.description: Remove redundant instructions, boilerplate, and verbose few-shot examples, or use a compression model to distill context into fewer tokens before sending.
techniques.example: Run long retrieved context through LLMLingua to compress it 2-5x before passing it to the model, preserving key information at a fraction of the tokens.

techniques.name: Output Length Control (max_tokens + concise instructions)
techniques.description: Cap max_tokens and instruct the model to be concise or return structured/JSON output. Output tokens are often priced 3-5x higher than input, so trimming them yields outsized savings.
techniques.example: Set max_tokens=150 and add 'Answer in one sentence' instead of letting the model emit a verbose multi-paragraph reply.

techniques.name: Request Batching
techniques.description: Combine multiple items into a single call, or use asynchronous batch APIs that offer deep discounts for non-latency-sensitive jobs.
techniques.savings: 50% cost reduction via batch APIs (OpenAI/Anthropic batch tiers)
techniques.example: Submit overnight classification of 100k records through OpenAI's Batch API at 50% of the synchronous price.

techniques.name: Streaming + Early Termination
techniques.description: Stream responses and stop generation as soon as the needed content (e.g. a parsed field or stop sequence) is produced, avoiding billing for unneeded trailing tokens.
techniques.example: Define a stop sequence of '}' when expecting a single JSON object so generation halts immediately after the object closes.

tools.name: Redis LangCache / Redis Semantic Cache
tools.description: Managed and open-source semantic caching layer for LLM responses using vector similarity; reported up to 73% cost reduction and major latency gains in high-repetition workloads.
tools.pricing_paid: Redis Cloud usage-based tiers; LangCache managed service priced per usage (free open-source Redis Stack available)

tools.name: GPTCache
tools.description: Open-source semantic cache for LLM queries supporting embedding-based similarity matching, pluggable vector stores, and multiple LLM backends.
tools.pricing_paid: Free (open source; you pay for your own storage/compute)

tools.name: LiteLLM
tools.description: Unified proxy/SDK for 100+ LLM providers with built-in caching, model routing/fallbacks, rate limiting, and cost tracking.
tools.pricing_paid: Open-source free; LiteLLM Enterprise from ~$250/mo for SSO, support, and advanced features

tools.name: Helicone
tools.description: LLM observability and gateway platform offering request logging, caching, cost analytics, and prompt management via a drop-in proxy.
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier (10k logs/mo); paid plans from ~$20/mo scaling with volume

tools.name: LangChain / LangCache integrations
tools.description: Framework for building LLM apps with built-in caching abstractions (in-memory, Redis, SQLite, semantic) and easy swapping of models and retrievers.

tools.name: LLMLingua
tools.description: Microsoft prompt-compression tool that uses a small model to compress prompts/context by up to 20x while retaining key information.

tools.name: Portkey
tools.description: AI gateway with semantic caching, model routing, load balancing, fallbacks, and observability across providers.

tools.name: Cloudflare AI Gateway
tools.description: Gateway that adds caching, rate limiting, logging, and analytics in front of LLM providers with minimal setup.
tools.pricing_paid: Free for core gateway features; usage-based for logs/analytics add-ons

quick_wins: Enable prompt caching by moving all static content (system prompt, tool defs, docs) to the front of your messages to capture up to 90% off cached prefix tokens.
Add an exact-match response cache (Redis key = prompt hash with temperature=0) to serve repeated identical calls for free.
Cap max_tokens and instruct the model to be concise, since output tokens cost 3-5x more than input.
Route easy/low-stakes requests to a cheaper model (e.g. GPT-4o-mini or Gemini Flash) via LiteLLM and reserve frontier models for hard cases.
Tighten RAG retrieval: add a reranker and lower top-k so you send only the few most relevant chunks instead of bulk context.
